{{Short description|Polish mathematician}}
'''Ludomir Newelski''' (born 27 November 1960, [[Wrocław]]) is a Polish mathematician, specializing in [[model theory]], [[set theory]], [[foundations of mathematics]], and [[universal algebra]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Ludomir Newelski, Professor|website=Institute of Mathematics, Polska Akademia Nauk (PAN)|url=https://www.impan.pl/~newelski}}</ref>

He attended the 14th High School in Wrocław, where in April 1977, as a second-year student, he became one of the first laureates of the Polish Mathematical Olympiad in this school. He studied and graduated in mathematics at the [[University of Wrocław]] and then worked at the Mathematical Institute of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (PAN). At PAN he received his PhD in 1987<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=139002}}</ref> and [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in 1991. He worked at PAN until 1994 and then moved to the University of Wrocław, where he now works. He obtained the rank of full professor in 1998.<ref name=homepage/> From 2007 to 2016 Newelski was the director of the Mathematical Institute of the University of Wrocław.

Newelski was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1998 in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Newelski, Ludomir|chapter=Meager forking and m-independence|title=Proc. Int. Congress of Math., 1998 Berlin|volume=2|year=1998|pages=33–42|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011639000}}</ref> He was the winner of the [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] in the field of exact sciences in 2001 "for work in the field of mathematical logic constituting a breakthrough in model theory and algebra".
